title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Realistic Scenarios Through Representation Engineering
abstract: arXiv:2610.29129v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reward hacking is a major problem in current production machine learning systems, resulting in costly and dangerous failures. Here we study how to monitor for and mitigate reward hacking in realistic settings, including tool calls and long contexts. We apply a dynamic intervention to steering directions obtained by three different methods: difference-in-means vectors from labeled rollouts, gradient optimization-based vectors, and vectors extracted when models reference an anti-reward-hacking model spec. This dynamic intervention perturbs model representations less than uniform steering vector addition to the residual stream, allowing for more precise edits. We find that we are able to cheaply and significantly reduce reward hacking without correspondingly significant costs to model coherence or capability, and that steering vectors originally extracted from coding environments also generalize to reducing reward hacking in other domains.

translated_title: 通过表征工程在现实场景中缓解奖励黑客行为
translated_abstract: 奖励黑客行为是当前生产级机器学习系统中的一个重大问题，会导致代价高昂且危险的故障。本研究探讨了如何在现实环境中（包括工具调用和长上下文）监测和缓解奖励黑客行为。我们对通过三种不同方法获得的引导方向应用了动态干预：来自标注回合数据的均值差向量、基于梯度优化的向量，以及模型引用反奖励黑客行为规范时提取的向量。这种动态干预比向残差流均匀添加引导向量对模型表征的扰动更小，从而能够实现更精确的编辑。我们发现，该方法能够以低成本显著减少奖励黑客行为，且不会对模型的连贯性或能力造成相应的显著损失；此外，最初从编程环境中提取的引导向量也能泛化到减少其他领域的奖励黑客行为。
tldr: 本研究提出一种基于表征工程的动态干预方法，通过多种引导向量以低成本显著减少现实场景中的奖励黑客行为，且不损害模型能力，并能跨领域泛化。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a dynamic representation engineering intervention using steering vectors that cheaply and significantly reduces reward hacking in realistic scenarios without compromising model coherence or capability, and generalizes across domains.
